summary: This bill requires the President to impose asset freezes and visa bans on foreign persons who commit or support violence, property destruction, or terrorism in the West Bank, or who lead entities involved in such acts.

scores.thoughts: The bill authorizes sanctions, reporting requirements, and administrative actions by the President, Treasury, and State Department. These functions involve negligible new federal spending and do not expand or reduce government budgets in any meaningful way.
The bill contains no provisions related to taxes, tax rates, or revenue policy.
The bill addresses foreign-policy sanctions and has no connection to healthcare systems or policy.
While the bill targets acts of violence, it does so exclusively through foreign sanctions and does not address domestic firearm regulations or gun rights.

Section 3(b)(2) mandates that covered foreign persons are inadmissible, ineligible for visas, and subject to visa revocation. This uses immigration enforcement tools to restrict entry, aligning directionally with the +1 pole of restricting immigration, though the measure is narrowly targeted at sanctioned individuals rather than broad immigration policy.
The bill has no provisions concerning reproductive rights or abortion access.
The bill does not alter military or defense spending levels.
No environmental or regulatory provisions are present.
The legislation does not address welfare programs or social safety-net policy.
No education-related content exists in the bill.
The bill contains no drug-policy provisions.
Although the bill references terrorism and violent acts, it applies sanctions to foreign persons abroad and does not modify U.S. criminal sentencing, policing, or rehabilitation policy.
Asset-blocking sanctions are economic measures but do not constitute changes to trade agreements, tariffs, or trade policy.
The bill has no fiscal or debt-related implications.
No provisions address LGBTQ+ legal protections.
The bill imposes sanctions rather than authorizing, expanding, or reducing foreign aid.
The legislation does not address voting access or election procedures.
No technology, data, or privacy regulations are included.
The bill has no labor or union-related content.
No provisions address religious exemptions or anti-discrimination law.
